questions.question: Who is Wiem?
questions.answer: Wiem Ben Salem is a software engineering student passionate about designing and building structured, scalable, and user-oriented applications. She specializes in full-stack development and application architecture, with experience across frontend, backend, databases, and DevOps.

questions.question: What kind of engineer is Wiem?
questions.answer: Wiem is a full-stack software engineer with strong backend and frontend capabilities. She works across the entire stack — from database design and API architecture to responsive user interfaces. Her strength lies in building complete systems where different components work together seamlessly.

questions.question: What is Wiem currently learning?
questions.answer: Wiem is currently pursuing Python certifications (FreeCodeCamp & PCAP), learning AWS Cloud Fundamentals including core services, IAM, and cost-aware architecture, and studying system design basics covering scalability, caching, and API design.

questions.question: What projects has Wiem worked on?
questions.answer: Wiem has worked on 6 projects. Her most recent and most substantial work is an AI Knowledge & HR Copilot with RAG-based search, built from scratch as the primary backend engineer, and MedFlow, a healthcare SaaS platform where she owned the prescription and localization domains. She has also built an Urban Traffic Management Platform with microservices, a Big Data Analytics Pipeline, TuniWay (tourism platform), and TravelTun (multi-platform tourism app).

questions.question: What is MedFlow?
questions.answer: MedFlow is a full-stack healthcare SaaS platform that digitizes the clinical workflow — from appointment booking through e-prescriptions and QR-verified pharmacy fulfillment, with role-based access and real-time doctor-patient messaging. It's built with Java 25, Spring Boot 4.1, React 19, PostgreSQL, and uses Docker Compose with GitLab CI/CD.

questions.question: What was Wiem's role in MedFlow?
questions.answer: Wiem was responsible for the prescription and localization areas of the MedFlow MVP. Her work included implementing electronic prescriptions with QR code generation, versioned fulfillment tracking, pharmacy module components with inventory management, and contributing to the real-time doctor-patient messaging system.

questions.question: What technologies were used in MedFlow?
questions.answer: MedFlow uses Java 25 with Spring Boot 4.1, Spring Security with OAuth2/JWT and Argon2 password hashing, PostgreSQL with Liquibase for migrations, React 19 with TypeScript, Vite 8, TailwindCSS 4, shadcn/ui, WebSocket/STOMP for real-time features, Docker Compose, GitLab CI/CD, and Gradle.

questions.question: What is the AI Knowledge & HR Copilot?
questions.answer: The AI Knowledge & HR Copilot is an internal AI assistant combining a RAG-based knowledge base with structured HR workflows. It features vector-search document retrieval with a two-layer hallucination-refusal system, CV extraction via Gemini, and candidate scoring with a deterministic skill-matching algorithm. It's built as a pnpm monorepo with NestJS 11 and Next.js 16.

questions.question: Tell me about Wiem's internships.
questions.answer: Wiem has completed three internships: at MedFlow (8 weeks, healthcare SaaS, prescription/pharmacy systems), at PlaySoft (8 weeks, built the AI Knowledge & HR Copilot with RAG pipeline), and at BeeCoders (end-of-studies, Flutter mobile app with Firebase).

questions.question: What did Wiem work on during her PlaySoft internship?
questions.answer: During her PlaySoft internship, Wiem built the AI Knowledge & HR Copilot — a full-stack pnpm monorepo combining a RAG-based knowledge base with structured HR workflows. She implemented the document embedding/vector-search pipeline (pgvector + HNSW), a two-layer hallucination-refusal system, CV extraction via Gemini, and candidate scoring with role-based access control.

questions.question: What technologies has Wiem used professionally?
questions.answer: In professional settings, Wiem has used Java 25, Spring Boot 4.1, Spring Security, PostgreSQL, React 19, TypeScript, WebSocket/STOMP, NestJS 11, Next.js 16, pgvector, Google Gemini API, TypeORM, pnpm Workspaces, Docker, GitLab CI/CD, Flutter, and Firebase.

questions.question: What frontend technologies does Wiem use?
questions.answer: Wiem's frontend technologies include Angular, React 19, Next.js, Flutter, TypeScript, TailwindCSS 4, shadcn/ui, and HTML/CSS. She has experience building responsive web applications and cross-platform mobile apps.

questions.question: What backend technologies does Wiem use?
questions.answer: Wiem's backend technologies include Java 25, Spring Boot 4.1, Spring Security, NestJS 11, Node.js, GraphQL, Python, .NET/ASP.NET Core, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, and Firebase. She has experience with REST APIs, GraphQL, WebSocket, and microservices architecture.

questions.question: Does Wiem have experience with databases?
questions.answer: Yes, Wiem has experience with multiple database systems: PostgreSQL (used in MedFlow, AI Knowledge & HR Copilot, and Urban Traffic), MySQL, MongoDB (used in TuniWay), and Firebase Firestore (used in TravelTun). She also has experience with pgvector for vector search and Liquibase for database migrations.

questions.question: Does Wiem have DevOps experience?
questions.answer: Yes, Wiem has DevOps experience including Docker and Docker Compose for containerization, GitLab CI/CD pipelines, GitHub Actions, and Linux administration (Ubuntu, Debian). She has used these tools across multiple professional and personal projects.
